reviewed_version: Publisher version of record, GAFA35(2025)43-112,70 physical PDF pages
summary: Theorem5.13 is false for continuous semialgebraic paths as stated: a terminal parameter-speed singularity at a regular hypersurface survives every permitted global power reparametrization. The defect is in the explicit finite-energy connector proof chain; the main metric-existence theorem is not disproved.

problems.title: Terminal speed singularity survives every asserted power reparametrization

source_claim.paraphrase: For every continuous semialgebraic gamma:[0,1]->P_n,d starting on Delta and outside Delta for all t in(0,1], there exists a positive integer m with gamma(s^m) of finite W2 energy.

suspect_step.description: After splitting the energy at r0, the proof infers boundedness on[r0,1] from regularity of the hypersurface equation, without controlling parameter derivatives.

hypotheses.verification: sqrt(1-t) is defined by u>=0,u^2=1-t; polynomial combinations remain semialgebraic and continuous. Gamma is smooth on[0,1).
p_0=z0^2 has a double projective root[0:1].
r(t)>0 and roots[+r(t):1],[-r(t):1] are distinct. The first gradient component at each affine root is +/-2r(t), nonzero; at t=1,r=1.

decisive_check.method: universal analytic proof with separate exact-arithmetic algebra checks
decisive_check.matching_justification: At each t>0 roots are separated. The uncrossed permutation has vanishing local cost, while the crossed permutation has positive limiting cost; the two-point transport linear program attains its minimum at a permutation.
decisive_check.normalization: Unit-sphere horizontal lift b(r)=(r,1)/sqrt(1+r^2), as in AppendixA.1, gives squared projective speed r'^2/(1+r^2)^2.
decisive_check.stated_result: Some permitted m gives finite quadratic energy.
decisive_check.actual_result: Every permitted m gives divergent integral; mu composed with gamma(s^m) is not AC2.
decisive_check.finite_computation_limit: The code checks polynomial identities and rational constants, not the universal theorem.

counterevidence_and_alternative_readings: The counterexample remains regular at the bad endpoint, so it does not violate the avoidance-of-discriminant condition.
Changing a homogeneous representative cannot alter the measure speed.
A C1 assumption including one-sided regularity at1 would exclude the example, but is absent from Theorem5.13.
A local theorem near0 is not refuted; the printed result is global on[0,1].
The exact publisher-page images and current public article HTML agree on the operative assumption.

correction.statement: For this gamma, phi(s)=1-(1-s)^2 is an endpoint-preserving strictly increasing semialgebraic reparametrization and gamma composed with phi has finite energy.

problems.decisive_source: Publisher version of record, Theorem 5.13 and its proof, physical PDF pages 44–45 (printed 86–87); Definitions 2.2 and 5.1, physical 15 and 35; projective metric normalization Appendix A.1, physical 64.
problems.independent_check: Root independently differentiates r(t)=t(1+sqrt(1-t)) and computes the horizontal projective speed of [r:1] as |r'|/(1+r^2). For two distinct roots the uncrossed matching has vanishing local cost and the crossed matching stays positive, so the measure speed squared is g=r'^2/(1+r^2)^2. With u=sqrt(1-t), r=1+u-u^2-u^3 and r'=-(1-2u-3u^2)/(2u); hence (1-t)g -> 1/16. For every integer m>=1, (1-s)|d(mu_(s^m))/ds|^2 -> m/16, using (1-s^m)/(1-s) -> m. Thus every permitted power gives infinite energy; this is an analytic all-m proof, not extrapolation from finite calculations.
problems.hypothesis_and_counterevidence_check: The polynomial z0^2-r(t)^2 z1^2 has a fixed nonzero leading coefficient, is a continuous semialgebraic projective path, has a double root only at t=0, and has two regular distinct roots for every t>0 including t=1. The theorem imposes neither n>=2 nor terminal C1 regularity. The source explicitly defines energy by ambient W2 metric speed; regularity of the hypersurface at t=1 does not bound coefficient derivatives. A theorem local near t=0 or strengthened by terminal C1 regularity is not refuted.
problems.repair_check: The example-only reparametrization phi(s)=1-(1-s)^2 gives r(phi)=4s-4s^2+s^3. Root independently expands and integrates its derivative square to 47/15; since the metric denominator is at least one, this supplies finite energy for the example. No general corrected theorem is certified.
problems.severity_reason: The false universally quantified Theorem 5.13 and the invalid boundedness step lie in the explicit Theorem 5.13 -> Corollary 5.14 -> Theorem 5.15 finite-energy connector derivation. This supports Major under the core-derivation calibration. The report properly avoids claiming the ultimate metric-existence or geodesicity conclusion false.
